title: POC quality eval + load scoping - Sunward Analytics
summary: Discovery-style scoping to define POC success metrics for QA/eval: golden prompt set, regression tests, hallucination detection thresholds, format checks, throughput/load targets. Agreed to run a two-week pilot with 10k sample transactions and a 48-hour benchmarking window. Next deliverables: benchmark plan, skeleton golden set, security questionnaire response.
next_steps: Redwood to send preliminary golden prompt template and scoring rubric by 2027-06-14
Sunward to provide 10k anonymized sample records (PII removed) by 2027-06-18
Schedule 48-hour benchmark window (tentative week of 2027-06-21) - Luca to propose exact slots
Redwood to fill security questionnaire and share SOC2/ISO summary by 2027-06-16
Follow-up call to review initial golden set and scoring results on 2027-06-20
action_items: Maya Chen - Share golden prompt template + scoring rubric - due 2027-06-14
Luca Moreno - Draft benchmark runbook and instance sizing recommendations - due 2027-06-15
Priya Nair - Deliver 10k anonymized sample payloads and top 500 golden candidates - due 2027-06-18
Omar Haddad - Confirm VPC egress and KMS requirements; share network diagram - due 2027-06-16
Sophie Lee - Collate product acceptance criteria and edge-case list for hallucination checks - due 2027-06-15
transcript: 00:00 Maya: Okay starting, everyone? Hi uh this is Maya from Redwood, thanks for joining. 00:05 Priya: Hey all, Priya here, thanks Maya. 00:08 Sophie: Sophie, hi. 00:09 Omar: Omar on the call. 00:12 Maya: Great quick agenda we'll scope a short POC around quality eval and load and agree success metrics, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination thresholds, and timeline. Luca will cover the benchmark plan. 00:24 Luca: Hi all, hi Priya, quick note I'm going to be a bit granular on the runbook and VM sizing later. 00:30 Priya: Sounds good. Couple context points from our side first: we're integrating LLM answers into our insights product for enterprise customers, must be under 400ms median latency for UI queries, and we have strict data residency needs in eu-west-1 for some customers. 00:45 Maya: Got it latency and residency - we'll note that. Is security a blocker for the POC or just later? 00:50 Priya: For POC it's not a blocker but we need SOC2 summary and KMS integration details, and any on-prem / VPC options if needed. 00:58 Maya: We'll share the security brief; Redwood Private options were touched earlier in the questionnaire. 01:03 Sophie: On success criteria — what does pass look like for you? We have a product acceptance doc but we'll refine. 01:10 Priya: Core success is three things: first precision on entity extraction and numeric normalization above 92% on golden cases; second hallucination rate below 2% measured on a curated golden set; third consistent latency under SLA for 95th percentile on web queries. 01:25 Omar: To add, we need deterministic output format for further downstream parsing, so format checks and schema validation must be automatic. 01:33 Luca: Okay so we have metrics: precision, hallucination rate, format compliance, latency p95. We'll map those into the eval rubric. 01:41 Maya: Let's talk golden prompts — do you have examples? 01:44 Priya: We have a handful, but need help expanding to edge cases. We'll share 500 initial golden candidates, Redwood to help grow to 2k and annotate. 01:54 Maya: That works. For the POC we typically propose a 'golden set' of 1-2k prompts with positive and negative cases, and a separate regression suite of 5-10k synthetic variants. 02:06 Omar: When you say synthetic variants can you explain? 02:09 Luca: Sure - synthetic variants are automated perturbations we generate to test robustness: ellipsis, truncated contexts, entity reorderings, noisy OCR artifacts. We also include adversarial paraphrases. 02:21 Omar: Good. Regarding hallucination checks, do you have an automated way to detect fabricated facts? 02:26 Luca: We combine pattern-based checks and citation-matching where possible. For structured output we do schema validation plus a fuzzy-lookup against customer-provided canonical records to catch invented IDs. It's not perfect but between fuzzy-matching and heuristics we get high signal. 02:40 Priya: What about scoring? How do you weight the metrics? 02:44 Maya: Typical approach we suggested: 40% correctness on golden prompts, 25% format compliance, 20% hallucination penalty (lower is better), 15% latency/throughput. But we can modify weights to match your business priorities. 02:57 Sophie: We'd likely push format compliance higher to 30% since downstream systems break on small schema changes. 03:03 Maya: Fine, we'll update rubric to 30/40/15/15 split and present it with examples. 03:11 Priya: For throughput sizing — our current peak is 250 qps for web UI across EU regions, average 80 qps. For the POC a scaled-down simulation of 100 qps sustained for 48 hours would be representative. 03:24 Luca: For 100 qps sustained with sequence lengths around 256 tokens, we recommend a cluster of 4 x A100-style workers or equivalent quantized config. We'll include memory and KV cache recommendations in the runbook. 03:36 Omar: Are you suggesting Dedicated or Hosted for the test? We prefer hosted to avoid infra setup but need VPC peering options and KMS integration. 03:45 Maya: Hosted with dedicated capacity or Redwood Private - for the POC hosted dedicated capacity is simplest: we can provision reserved-ish capacity and enable VPC peering for secure egress. KMS for key wrapping supported via customer KMS through an envelope flow. 03:58 Priya: Any concerns about data residency? 04:00 Luca: We'll ensure the POC runs in eu-west-1 and metadata and logs can be restricted to that region. We'll note any cross-region fallbacks are disabled for the run. 04:10 Sophie: Walk me through the benchmark window logistics. 04:13 Luca: We propose a 48-hour window. First 4 hours are warmup with mixed load, then a 40-hour steady-state run at target qps, and final 4 hours of ramp-down and failure modes like model swap and partial node loss to observe graceful degradation. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, error rates, and tail-latency distributions. 04:34 Priya: For graceful degradation what fallback models do you use? 04:37 Maya: We can route to a cheaper quantized variant or to a smaller model with precomputed cache responses for top queries. We'll document exact policies. 04:45 Omar: How do you capture hallucination during the run? 04:47 Luca: We run background evals on a held-out golden set every 2 hours and produce a hallucination-stats dashboard plus sample cases flagged for manual review. 04:58 Priya: Manual review — how much effort do you expect from our team? 05:01 Maya: For the POC we usually ask customers to review top 200 flagged cases; Redwood will pre-filter and annotate confidence tiers to minimize review load. 05:11 Sophie: On regression testing - how do you ensure future model updates don't break QA? 05:15 Luca: We create a regression playlist — a ranked list of golden and negative cases that must be re-run on every model rollout in staging. We set acceptance gates and automatic rollback if key metrics degrade. 05:27 Priya: Nice, can we sample for hallucination by type? Like numbers/IDs vs invented entities? 05:31 Luca: Yes we tag hallucinations by category during evaluation and provide per-category thresholds for acceptance. 05:39 Omar: I want more detail on format checks — what validators do you use? 05:43 Luca: JSON schema validation, type checks, length constraints, and regex patterns for IDs. We also run downstream parsers as part of the pipeline to catch integration breaks. 05:52 Priya: Any caveats with quantization and hallucination? 05:55 Luca: Quantization sometimes affects factuality subtly; we'll recommend baseline quality runs comparing float32 vs quantized int8/4 variants and include those in the scoring. 06:05 Maya: On timelines, proposed schedule: initial artifacts exchanged by 2027-06-18, benchmark run week of 2027-06-21, results review 2027-06-24, pilot wrap + decision by 2027-06-30. 06:18 Priya: That timeline aligns with our internal roadmap. 06:21 Sophie: For acceptance thresholds — double-check the hallucination 2% number; how measured? 06:25 Luca: Measured as number of outputs with at least one hallucinated fact over total evaluated outputs on the curated golden set, using both exact-match and fuzzy checks plus manual labeling for uncertain cases. 06:38 Omar: Regarding costs, can you provide an estimate for the 48-hour benchmark including dedicated infra? 06:43 Luca: We'll produce a cost estimate: infra hours, model token costs, and Redwood engineering support hours. Estimate sent with benchmark runbook. 06:52 Priya: On security docs, send SOC2 report and network integration guide. Also confirm RBAC and audit logging retention options. 06:59 Maya: We'll include audit log retention settings and RBAC mappings; we support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning. 07:08 Sophie: Are there any limitations around streaming and function calls we should know? 07:13 Luca: Streaming works with same SLOs; function/tool calling uses structured outputs and we recommend testing end-to-end for any tool invocation during the POC. 07:21 Priya: A few transcript oddities earlier — sorry if my example dataset had a few OCR artefacts. 07:25 Omar: No worries. 07:27 Maya: To confirm next steps: Redwood sends golden prompt template + rubric, Luca shares runbook and size recs, Sunward supplies sample set and product acceptance doc, then benchmark scheduling. 07:36 Sophie: I'll compile acceptance doc and edge-case list. 07:40 Priya: We'll anonymize and send samples by the 18th. 07:43 Maya: Great, I'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and the 6/20 review. 07:49 Luca: One last technical note: for KV cache warmup during the 4-hour warmup we recommend seeding caches with top 10k recent queries to avoid cold-start penalties. 07:59 Omar: Good call. 08:01 Maya: Any final questions? 08:03 Priya: None from me, thanks. 08:05 Sophie: Thanks, bye. 08:06 Omar: Bye. 08:07 Maya: Thanks everyone, talk soon. 08:10 Speaker 1: [unintelligible] end of call.
